original_title: The Next Film From Disney and Pixar is a Crime Movie set in Italy… with Cats
summary_en: Disney and Pixar are diving into the world of organized crime with their next animated feature, 'Gatto.' Set against the picturesque backdrop of Venice, the film promises a unique blend of feline capers and existential musings.
ai_analysis: This animated crime comedy offers a fresh, genre-bending approach from Pixar, potentially appealing to adult audiences who appreciate sophisticated storytelling within animation.

en.title: Pixar Unleashes Cat-tastic Crime Comedy 'Gatto' in Venice
en.summary: Disney and Pixar are diving into the world of organized crime with their next animated feature, 'Gatto.' Set against the picturesque backdrop of Venice, the film promises a unique blend of feline capers and existential musings.
en.body:
Get ready for a whisker-twitching adventure as Disney and Pixar prepare to roll out their latest animated feature, **Gatto**. This isn't your typical heartwarming tale; instead, the studio is venturing into the gritty, yet charming, world of gangster comedies, all set against the iconic canals and alleyways of Venice, Italy. The film's premise centers on **Nero**, a scrawny, impoverished black cat voiced by **Mark Ruffalo**. Pulled into the orbit of a powerful, and decidedly feline, crime family, Nero finds himself tasked with dangerous heists for the formidable crime boss **Rocco**.

As Nero navigates the perilous life of a thief, he begins to ponder the meaning of his existence, questioning if his nine lives are being wasted on a life of crime. This existential crisis is at the heart of **Gatto**, exploring themes of purpose and redemption through the eyes of its animated protagonists. The film is directed by **Enrico Casarosa**, who previously helmed the beloved Pixar film **Luca**, also set in Italy. Casarosa’s passion for his homeland is evident, and he’s assembled an impressive voice cast to bring this unique story to life.

## A Purrfectly Italian Mob Story

The vibrant setting of Venice serves as more than just a backdrop; it’s an integral part of the film's atmosphere, promising a visually stunning experience. The teaser hints at a world where cats are the primary inhabitants, with a few other creatures like rodents and pigeons making appearances. This anthropomorphic approach allows Pixar to explore classic crime drama tropes with a playful, family-friendly twist. The narrative seems poised to balance thrilling heists and the inherent dangers of the criminal underworld with the emotional journey of Nero as he seeks a life of greater meaning. Will he escape Rocco's clutches and find his true calling amidst the Venetian labyrinth?

## A Star-Studded Feline Ensemble

The voice cast for **Gatto** is nothing short of spectacular, featuring a roster of acclaimed actors. Alongside **Mark Ruffalo** as the protagonist Nero, the film boasts performances from **Laurence Fishburne**, **John Turturro**, **Isabella Rossellini**, **Natasia Demetriou**, **Jamie Demetriou**, **Jason Schwartzman**, **Rhys Darby**, and **Tracey Ullman**, among others. The presence of **Enrico Casarosa** himself in the voice cast further underscores the personal connection to this project. This ensemble promises nuanced performances that will bring depth and personality to the film's diverse cast of cat characters, making their struggles and triumphs all the more engaging for audiences.

## What's Next

**Gatto** is slated for a theatrical release on March 5, 2027. Fans eager to see Pixar tackle a new genre with such a distinctive premise will want to keep an eye out for further trailers and sneak peeks as the release date approaches.

content_raw: Listen up, wiseguys. There’s a new Disney/Pixar movie coming out, and it’s a crime movie! Specifically, it’s a movie about the Italian mob. It takes place in Venice, Italy, and is the story of a scrawny, impoverished young fellow named Nero (voiced by Mark Ruffalo) who is taken in by a powerful crime family. In exchange for this, his job is to steal things for them… often at great personal risk. Also, they’re all cats. Everybody’s a cat. Well, a couple of characters seem to be rodents. And there’s a pigeon, I think. But it’s mostly cats. The film is titled Gatto (which is Italian for “cat”). Anyway, Nero starts to find himself in very dangerous situations, working as a thief for the (literal) fat cat crime boss Rocco, and learns that he has nine lives that he’s wasting, dying while doing criminal errands. Thus, he asks himself the great questions many crime movie protagonists ask themselves: is everything he’s doing worth it? Is he living a life that’s worth living as if it’s his only one? How can he change his life so that it’s full of meaning? In addition to Ruffalo, the voice cast includes: Laurence Fishburne, Enrico Casarosa (who also directs), John Turturro, Isabella Rossellini, Natasia Demetriou, Jamie Demetriou, Jason Schwartzman, Saverio Raimondo, Jason Mantzoukas, Tracey Ullman, Marco Calvani, and Rhys Darby. Perhaps it’s a great film to take your children to as you start to introduce them to the “mafia movie” genre. Watch Gatto and then The Godfather and find out which one they like better! The film will be in theaters next March. Ci vediamo!
